leaks.h2a: Five ways a brand ends up
leaks.lede: A brand is built in a sequence. Each stage below is where brands lose their edge, and how we build it.

stages.breaks: Designing a logo before deciding what the brand stands for.
stages.why: A logo cannot fix an unclear idea. Without a position, every later choice is a matter of taste.
stages.does: We start with audience, promise and competitors, and write a clear position that every later decision can be checked against.

stages.breaks: Choosing a name because it is available.
stages.why: A name is used in every conversation. It needs to be easy to say, spell and remember, and not confuse a buyer.
stages.does: We generate and test name options against meaning, sound, availability and how they read in your markets.

stages.breaks: Copying a category look so you blend in.
stages.why: If your brand looks like every other brand in the category, buyers cannot tell you apart.
stages.does: We design a logo, colour and typography that fit your position and stand apart from the category.

stages.breaks: Writing every message in a different tone.
stages.why: Inconsistent words make a brand feel less trustworthy, however good the design is.
stages.does: We define how the brand speaks, with examples for headlines, ads, emails and support, so anyone can write in its voice.

stages.breaks: Handing over a logo file and nothing else.
stages.why: Without rules and templates, the brand drifts as more people and agencies touch it.
stages.does: We deliver guidelines and ready-to-use templates for the places the brand appears, and help you roll them out.

numbers.note: The deliverables, in the order we build them.
